gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build step is the smallest honest place to widen runtime pilot coverage from atomic64 and bitmap into the trace-events sample lane.
A trace-events survey gate keeps the Linux sample anchor, starter status, and remaining runtime-substrate blocker explicit while the pilot surface stays small.
A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing trace-events step that can model event emission and callback registration without pretending full macro or thread parity exists.
A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter sample reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions, event emission counts, and registration balance.
The next meaningful step is a tiny table-driven payload gate that replays a few foo_bar, template, and function-callback expectations from the Linux sample before widening the starter.
A loadable module entry point, thread creation, and tracepoint registration parity still depend on runtime substrate pieces that the repo has not started yet.
